s: The Birthday of Swami Vivekananda i.e 12th August is celebrated as?
The best representative of Neo-Hinduism in the second half of the nineteenth century was –
x: Swami Vivekananda (1863-1902 A.D.) was credited to interpret the teachings of Ramakrishna Paramahans. He described these teachings in simple language. Swami Vivekananda emerged as the advocate of Neo-Hinduism. In 1893 A.D., he went to Chicago, where he delivered his famous speech in ‘Parliament of the world's Religions.’ In his speech, Vivekananda gave a short introduction of Hinduism and spoke on “The meaning of the Hindu religion.” After that, he visited United States of America and England and promoted Hinduism. According to him, the Hindu religion was restricted up to food only. He was quite displeased with the silence of religion on the exploitation of the poor by the wealthy. Vivekananda never used to give political messages but still he brought the spirit of self-dignity among the new generation by his articles and speeches. He was a staunch patriot. Subhas Chandra Bose said about him, ‘so far as Bengal is concerned, Swami Vivekananda may be regarded as the spiritual father of the modern nationalist movement.

s: Who founded the ‘Theosophical Society’?
x: The Theosophical Society was founded in the year 1875 in New York City by Russian (Now-Ukrainian) noblewoman Helena Petrovna Blavatsky and American Colonel Henry Steel Alcott, along with William Quan Judge and some other individuals. In 1879, the principal founders, Madame H.P. Blavatsky and Col. Alcott moved to India where the Society spread rapidly. In 1882, they established the Society’s International Headquarter in Adyar, a suburb of Madras (currently Chennai). Brahmo Sabha was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828 and Ramkrishna Mission was founded by Swami Vivekananda in 1897, Thus, option (a) is correct.

s: The success of the Theosophical Society in India was mainly due to –
x: In 1879, the principal founders, Madam H.P. Blavatsky and Colonel Alcott, moved to India, where Theosophical Society spread rapidly. In 1882 A.D., they established the society’s international headquarters in Adyar, a suburb of Madras (currently Chennai). In 1889 A.D., Annie Besant joined the society, and after coming to India in 1893 A.D., she played an active role in society. She considered Hinduism to be the world’s most esoteric and spiritual religion. She used to believe in the principles of rebirth.

s: The Theosophical Society was led by
x: Annie Besant led the Theosophical Society in India and became its President in 1907 after Olcott's death. Hume, Griffith and Dufferin had no leadership role in it.

x: first here. Rabindranath Tagore composed Jana Gana Mana in 1911. During his tour of South India in 1919, he stayed at the Theosophical College in Madanapalle, Andhra Pradesh, from 25 th February to 2 March, after being fatigued from Modern Indian History PMF IAS IH – 133 travel. While in Madanapalle, Tagore translated Jana Gana Mana into English as "Morning Song of India" on 28 th February 1919. It was here that Margaret Cousins, wife of James Cousins and then principal of the college, set the composition to music, transforming it from a lyric into a song. Tagore was deeply impressed by the institution and referred to the Madanapalle Theosophical College as the "Shantiniketan of South India." Eventually, Jana Gana Mana was officially adopted as India's national anthem on 24 th January 1950.

s: Chief centre of Wahabi Movement during 19th century was:
x: Wahabi Movement offered a serious and organized threat to British supremacy in India during the 19th century. The movement was led by Syed Ahmad Barelavi, who was greatly influenced by the teachings of Abdul Wahab of Arabia and Shah Walliullah, the saint of Delhi. It was a revivalist movement that stated that the return to the true spirit of Islam was the only way to get rid of the socio-political oppression. Through the efforts of Syed Ahmad, Wahabi ideology was spread in Kabul, North-West Frontier Province, Bengal, Bihar and Central Provincial regions. In 1830 A.D. Patna became the centre of the Wahabi Movement after the death of Syed Ahmad.
